name: Medulloblastoma with Extensive Nodularity

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Tumors of the Central Nervous System (2021)

criteria.description: Presence of extensive nodularity with reticulin-free zones on histopathological examination
MRI demonstrating cerebellar mass with characteristic nodular appearance and cystic components
Molecular profiling consistent with SHH-activated medulloblastoma subgroup
Symptoms consistent with posterior fossa tumor such as ataxia and increased intracranial pressure

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of extensive nodularity plus either characteristic MRI findings or molecular subgrouping consistent with SHH activation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Molecular subgrouping is essential for accurate classification and prognosis.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Headache due to increased intracranial pressure
searchTerms: head pain from increased intracranial pressure

common.symptomName: Nausea and vomiting secondary to raised intracranial pressure
searchTerms: vomiting caused by increased intracranial pressure
eye exam shows optic disc swelling

common.symptomName: Lethargy and decreased level of consciousness

searchTerms: lack of coordination in finger-to-nose test

occasional.symptomName: Diplopia due to cranial nerve VI palsy
searchTerms: double vision from sixth nerve palsy
irritability in babies from fluid buildup

occasional.symptomName: Seizures (rare in medulloblastoma but occasionally reported)

rare.symptomName: Endocrine dysfunction secondary to hypothalamic involvement
searchTerms: endocrine dysfunction caused by brain lesion

rare.symptomName: Hearing loss due to brainstem compression
searchTerms: difficulty hearing due to nerve compression

rare.symptomName: Behavioral changes including irritability and mood swings

laboratory: CSF cytology may reveal tumor cells in metastatic cases
Elevated intracranial pressure on lumbar puncture opening pressure
imaging: MRI showing cerebellar mass with extensive nodularity and cystic components
T2-weighted hyperintense nodules with reticulin-free zones on histopathology correlated imaging
other: Histopathology demonstrating extensive nodularity with reticulin-free zones
Immunohistochemistry positive for synaptophysin and NeuN

distinguishingFeatures: Distinct cystic lesion with mural nodule on imaging
Loss of INI1 expression on immunohistochemistry

redFlags: Signs of increased intracranial pressure such as persistent vomiting and papilledema
New onset seizures or altered consciousness
references: Louis DN et al. WHO Classification of Tumors of the Central Nervous System, 5th Edition, 2021.
Ellison DW et al. Medulloblastoma: molecular subgroups and clinical implications. Nat Rev Clin Oncol. 2014.
